A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hybrid SNN–ANN object-detection study. Their complete main text, supplementary material, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gen1/Gen4 detection results, component ablations, computational analyses and Loihi 2 hardware measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains the original detection experiments, ablations and hardware measurements, including supplementary results.

M1.justification: The PLIF SNN backbone, SAT/ERS attention bridge, ANN blocks, optional DWConvLSTMs and YOLOX head are unchanged. Renaming the bridge output from F_out to E_feature in Equation 6 does not change its computation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gen1 and Gen4 automotive detection datasets, object classes and evaluation scenarios. No additional dataset, task or population is evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same ANN/GNN, SNN and RNN/SSM comparators, and Table 6 retains the same internal comparison variants. The Jetson hardware comparison also remains; its datasheet citation is updated.

E3.justification: The stated training budgets, batch sizes, learning rates, augmentations, 5 ms event bins and mAP metrics match. Hardware input sizes and quantization settings are also unchanged; the new resource acknowledgments do not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The attention, quantization, DWConvLSTM and SNN/ANN layer-count ablations are retained, as are the qualitative comparisons. The added supplementary references to Table 11 and Figure 6 point to evidence already present in v2.

E5.justification: Both versions report hardware means and standard deviations using 12 inputs and 100k steps in Tables 5 and 10. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The benchmark, ablation, complexity and hardware values match. Hybrid mAP remains 0.35 on Gen1 and 0.27 on Gen4, with 0.43 for Hybrid+RNN on Gen1. Figures 3 and 6 contain identical qualitative detection images.

T1.justification: The event representation, neuron dynamics, attention operations and hardware-conversion equations retain the same mathematics. Equation 6 changes only its output symbol; no definitions, derivations or proofs are substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same hybrid-detection novelty claim, attention-bridge and multi-timescale contributions, performance claims and neuromorphic-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of sparsity, attention, recurrent timescales and accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs remain unchanged. The hardware input-simulation limitation is retained; Section 3.1 merely rephrases the existing sparse-processing rationale.

D1.justification: v4 newly acknowledges JUWELS access through project neuroml and Intel-provided Loihi 2 access. This adds resource provenance, while implementation, hyperparameter and training-time disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds a JUWELS systems publication to the references. The Jetson datasheet reference is updated, while the related-work discussion and relationships to prior detection and hybrid-network research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited wording edits, adds author-contribution footnotes, revises affiliations and acknowledgments, and simplifies supplementary headings. It also adds explicit figure/table cross-references and renames the bridge output symbol without substantially rewriting the narrative.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn with revised styling and labels, including an explicit Detections label in Figure 1 and vector artwork in Figure 2. Table 6 moves between columns, with surrounding text reflow; the other figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves presentation and traceability through vector attention diagrams, clearer references to existing supplementary evidence, and explicit author/resource attribution. Scientific methods and empirical support are unchanged. The cleanup remains incomplete: Equation 6 uses E_feature while surrounding prose retains F_out, limiting the overall gain.
